name: manual_287e59
claim: Recovery from a backward-clock alarm is an audited administrative action: require an authenticated operator and trusted-time evidence, append the previous and accepted timestamps to an append-only log, reset the mark to the accepted time, and mark every reservation already expired at the old mark as expired for good. The approved default skew is zero; slewing never steps backward and needs no tolerance, and any non-zero tolerance needs a policy amendment.

decisions.notes: 2026-10-19: the approved clock policy was read only after a first implementation that cleared a quarantine with a name alone; it could have revived an expired reservation. Reading the policy found the gap before merge.
